---
title: "Glider Performance Tool"
---

Tools for choosing the right PAM glider for a study and planning its mission: what each
platform can carry, how the platforms compare, how long a glider will last on a given
mission, and where it can fly.

## How the project started

The project began at the **NOAA Fisheries Glider Rodeo 2026** hackathon as a way to compare
the PAM-equipped gliders that flew in the rodeo: how each platform was piloted, how well it
navigated, how long its battery and storage lasted, and how much noise it made. While building
that comparison it became clear that the same knowledge answers a bigger question that comes
before any deployment: *which glider, sensors and mission set-up suit this study?* The tool
has grown from a rodeo comparison into a general glider comparison and mission planning tool.

## The pages

**From the rodeo**

- [Glider Performance](content/performance.qmd): what every glider actually did during the
  rodeo, split by mission mode. This is the only page built directly on rodeo data.

**For choosing a glider and planning a mission**

- [Glider Selection Dashboard](content/glider-selection.qmd): enter what the mission needs
  (depth, duration, sensors, PAM recorder) and see which gliders match.
- [Direct Comparison](content/direct-comparison.qmd): Slocum and Seaglider factor by factor,
  from the pilots' experience.
- [Study Design Tool](content/study-design.qmd): draw a study area, lay out
  transects, estimate survey distance and mission duration, check the bathymetry, and export
  waypoint files.
- Endurance calculation for [Slocum](content/slocum-endurance.qmd) and
  [Seaglider](content/seaglider-endurance.qmd): how long a mission lasts with a given set of
  sensors and dive settings.

## The Glider Rodeo

The Glider Rodeo field-tested PAM-glider platforms under the same conditions to give
data-driven guidance on what each system can do in different operational environments and for
different research questions. Seven gliders from four platform types flew the same trackline
off the coast of Hawaii in January–February 2026:

| Glider | Platform | PAM system |
|---|---|---|
| risso, stenella, capex987 | Teledyne Webb Slocum G3S | DMON2, WISPR 3.0, JASCO OceanObserver |
| sg607, sg274 | Seaglider M1 / SGX | WISPR 3.0 |
| SEA117 | ALSEAMAR SeaExplorer | Auris |
| belladonna | Hefring Oceanscout | WISPR 6.1 |

Each glider was flown through a sequence of mission modes:

| Phase | Mode                     | Start (UTC)      | Stop (UTC)       |
|-------|--------------------------|------------------|------------------|
| 1     | shakedown                | 2026-01-28 22:00 | 2026-01-30 06:00 |
| 2     | fast                     | 2026-01-30 06:00 | 2026-02-01 18:00 |
| 3     | slow                     | 2026-02-01 18:00 | 2026-02-04 18:00 |
| 4     | intermediate             | 2026-02-04 18:00 | 2026-02-06 18:00 |
| 5     | drift (20 min at 800 m)  | 2026-02-06 18:00 | 2026-02-08 18:00 |
| 6     | mini-rodeo: slow         | 2026-02-08 18:00 | 2026-02-09 06:00 |
| 6     | mini-rodeo: intermediate | 2026-02-09 06:00 | 2026-02-09 18:00 |
| 6     | mini-rodeo: fast         | 2026-02-09 18:00 | 2026-02-10 06:00 |
| 7     | recovery                 | 2026-02-10 06:00 |                  |

Source: [Glider Rodeo fieldwork plan](https://nmfs-pam-glider.github.io/GliderRodeo/content/fieldwork.html).

### Rodeo datasets

- **Glider Rodeo deployment data** (engineering, science, GPS): on the Glider Rodeo JupyterHub
  in `shared-public/GliderRodeo/`, one folder per deployment.
- **Soundscape metrics** (60 s averaged spectra per glider): `shared-public/GliderRodeo/Noise/`.
- **Glider specifications:** `shared-public/GliderRodeo/PAM_Glider_Specs.csv`.

The source data are preliminary.
